title: A Semester for the Playlist
premise: Gideon Marchetti, a nonbinary debate champion hiding their identity from a hostile household, discovers their late grandmother's recipe box contains coded instructions to a hidden life she once lived under a different name. Following the recipes' clues through one final semester, Gideon uncovers a community of people their grandmother sheltered and a trust meant for 'whoever needs to become themselves.' As graduation looms and their family closes in on the secret, Gideon must choose between the safe, invisible future they've scripted and claiming the name, community, and voice they've been rehearsing all along.
about_author: Quentin Blackwood is the pen name of a former high-school debate coach who spent a decade watching teenagers argue brilliantly about everything except themselves. They write in a converted pantry, surrounded by recipe cards of mysterious origin.

chapters.title: Ninety-Seven Days
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Opening at a debate tournament win they can't celebrate at home, establishing the countdown calendar to graduation and the suffocating silence around their identity. Emotional beat: weary resignation masked as ambition.

chapters.title: The Recipe Box
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Clearing out grandma Rosa's kitchen after the funeral, Gideon finds cards that read like instructions but aren't: 'Fold in the name you buried. Bake until it stops hurting.' Emotional beat: eerie curiosity piercing grief.

chapters.title: Card Number One
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. The first card leads to a laundromat on Delancey Street where an old attendant recognizes 'Rosa's kid' and hands over a locker key. Emotional beat: the thrill of being seen by a stranger who expects nothing.

chapters.title: Debate Club, After Hours
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Gideon's best friend and debate partner notices Gideon flinching at home-life questions and starts quietly investigating why the champion never argues for themself. Emotional beat: loyal suspicion, love expressed as attention.

chapters.title: What Rosa Left Behind
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. The locker holds photos of grandma with strangers—runaways, drag performers, a teenage Rosa in men's clothing, 1962. Emotional beat: vertigo as the grandmother Gideon knew dissolves into someone braver.

chapters.title: Dinner Table Tactics
chapters.summary: Marcus (father)'s POV. Dad senses Gideon drifting and doubles down on control—college plans, curfews, 'the right path.' His chapter reveals fear disguised as discipline. Emotional beat: tragic misdirected protectiveness.

chapters.title: The Wednesday Circle
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Card three leads to a basement community center where Rosa once hosted meetings; the group still gathers, keeping her promise alive. Emotional beat: tentative belonging, like testing ice before trusting it.

chapters.title: Rehearsal
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya follows Gideon to the center, confronts them gently, and becomes co-conspirator. She asks what name Gideon would choose if no one was listening. Emotional beat: the terrifying tenderness of being asked directly.

chapters.title: Midterms and Misdirection
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Balancing secret visits, debate regionals prep, and a father growing suspicious of unexplained absences. A near-miss at home forces Gideon to hide the box. Emotional beat: adrenaline of double life beginning to cost sleep.

chapters.title: The Trust
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. The final card references a lawyer; documents reveal Rosa left a modest fund 'for whoever needs to become themselves,' contingent on a letter Gideon must write declaring who they are. Emotional beat: hope entangled with dread—the letter is the trap and the gift.

chapters.title: Blank Page
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Gideon tries and fails to write the letter across several nights, tearing up drafts. Flashbacks to childhood moments of self-recognition. Emotional beat: paralysis; survival habits fighting the truth.

chapters.title: Opposition Research
chapters.summary: Marcus's POV. Dad finds a discarded draft—not the letter, but a note in Gideon's handwriting using a different name—and begins his own investigation, contacting relatives. Emotional beat: dread building on both sides of the house.

chapters.title: Regionals
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. At the tournament, Gideon abandons their prepared case mid-round and argues something true instead, losing on points but winning something larger. Priya watches them transform. Emotional beat: exhilaration with consequences incoming.

chapters.title: The Phone Call
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. An aunt tips off Dad; he confronts Gideon with the note. The argument at home finally happens—the one Gideon could never win. Emotional beat: devastation, but also the strange relief of the secret being out.

chapters.title: Locked Out
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Kicked out for a night, Gideon lands at the Wednesday Circle, which becomes the family Rosa promised it would be. Emotional beat: rock bottom revealing a floor that holds.

chapters.title: Rosa's Letter
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. The lawyer produces a letter Rosa wrote years ago, addressed to 'my grandchild, whoever you turn out to be.' It names Gideon's struggle before Gideon could. Emotional beat: catharsis; grief and inheritance merging.

chapters.title: Counterargument
chapters.summary: Marcus's POV. Dad spirals—consulting his own memories of Rosa, discovering she protected him too from things he never knew. Emotional beat: cracks in certainty; the first flicker of reconsideration.

chapters.title: The Final Round
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. State championship: Gideon chooses to speak under their chosen name, publicly, with Priya beside them. The room's reaction is mixed but real. Emotional beat: climax—claiming identity at maximum stakes.

chapters.title: Homecoming
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Dad shows up outside the tournament, not to apologize fully but to listen—an imperfect truce offered in his clumsy language. Emotional beat: cautious, unfinished reconciliation.

chapters.title: Graduation Day
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. The ceremony; Gideon walks as themself, name read aloud correctly. The countdown calendar's last page is torn off. Emotional beat: quiet triumph, the sentence served and commuted at once.

chapters.title: The New Recipe Box
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Gideon adds their own first card to Rosa's box—a direction for whoever opens it next—and takes a small role keeping the Wednesday Circle alive. Emotional beat: becoming the ancestor someone else will need.

chapters.title: Whoever You Turn Out to Be
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV, epilogue. Summer's first morning: college forms filled out with the right name, a visit to Rosa's grave, the letter finally written and filed. Emotional beat: peace earned, identity no longer a debate but a fact.
